_help: How CVs and cover letters are written: by market (the posting's country) and by position type (six academic, four industry). engine/conventions.py picks both for each posting; you can tune each type in the app's Writing style tab (saved in inputs/document_conventions.json as 'types') and change the type or market of one posting in the Documents tab. A market's must_not_contain list is checked like tailoring_checks. These are common practice, not law; when a posting asks for something specific, the posting wins.

nordic.label: Nordic (Sweden, Norway, Denmark, Finland, Iceland)
nordic.spelling: British English (or the local language if the posting is in it)
nordic.photo: usually omitted (more common in Denmark); never needed
nordic.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, city; no date of birth, marital status, ID number or photo unless asked
nordic.work_authorization: state it briefly if you are not an EU/EEA citizen (for example permanent residence)
nordic.tone: factual, modest and concrete; no superlatives or self-promotion; show collaboration and how you work
nordic.metrics: sparingly: only verified results that the posting values; research postings welcome one or two per project
nordic.profile_section: a short profile of 3-4 lines is usual
nordic.references: 'References available upon request' is acceptable; names only when asked

letter.salutation: Dear Hiring Manager, (or the contact person's name)
letter.focus: why this employer and team, what you would contribute, how you work with others; avoid repeating the CV

nordic.language: write in the posting's language; Swedish/Norwegian/Danish postings usually expect the local language unless they say English is fine
notes: Employers value balance, teamwork and practical results more than personal branding.

dach.label: Germany, Austria, Switzerland
dach.spelling: British or US English used consistently; German if the posting is in German
dach.date_format: MM/YYYY in the CV, DD.MM.YYYY in the letter
dach.photo: traditionally common in Germany and Austria, but optional and not legally required; omit for international companies
dach.personal_details: name, address, phone, e-mail; date of birth and nationality are traditional but optional
dach.work_authorization: state it if you are not an EU/EEA (or Swiss) citizen
dach.tone: formal, precise, complete; exact dates; no unexplained gaps
dach.references: not listed; work certificates (Arbeitszeugnisse) and degree certificates are often attached

letter.focus: formal motivation letter (Anschreiben): position, qualifications that match, earliest start date and salary expectation if the posting asks

dach.language: German postings expect German documents unless English is stated
notes: A traditional German CV (Lebenslauf) is tabular, reverse-chronological, and ends with place, date and signature; international employers do not expect the signature.

uk_ie.label: United Kingdom and Ireland
uk_ie.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, town; omit date of birth, age, marital status, photo (UK equality law makes employers avoid these)
uk_ie.work_authorization: state right to work or visa status if relevant
uk_ie.profile_section: a personal profile/statement of 3-5 lines at the top is usual
uk_ie.references: 'References available on request', or two referees when asked

letter.closing: Yours sincerely, (with a name) / Kind regards,
letter.focus: match the essential criteria of the job description point by point

notes: Public sector and university posts often require a supporting statement that addresses each criterion of the person specification.

us.label: United States
us.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, city and state, LinkedIn/portfolio; never date of birth, age, photo, marital status, nationality or religion (US equal-employment rules make employers avoid them)
us.work_authorization: state visa or sponsorship needs only when relevant, briefly (for example 'Requires H-1B sponsorship')
us.tone: confident and achievement-oriented; every bullet starts with an action verb
us.metrics: expected: quantify impact (%, time, cost, scale, performance) wherever the material verifies it
us.profile_section: a 2-3 line summary is optional; skills section with the posting's exact keywords (applicant tracking systems)
us.references: omit; never write 'References available upon request'

letter.focus: the value you bring to the team's problems; direct and specific

notes: Industry uses a 'resume'; 'CV' means the long academic document. Use the posting's terminology for titles and skills so applicant tracking systems match them.

canada.label: Canada
canada.spelling: Canadian English (British-style spellings such as 'colour', '-ize' accepted)
canada.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, city and province; no date of birth, age, photo, marital status (human-rights codes)
canada.work_authorization: state citizenship, permanent residence or work permit status briefly if relevant
canada.tone: professional and achievement-oriented, somewhat less assertive than the US
canada.profile_section: short summary of qualifications is usual

letter.focus: fit with the role and the organization

canada.language: English; in Quebec, French is expected unless the posting is in English

australia_nz.label: Australia and New Zealand
australia_nz.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, suburb/city; no date of birth, age, photo, marital status
australia_nz.work_authorization: state citizenship, permanent residency or visa (with work rights) clearly; it is often asked
australia_nz.profile_section: a career summary/objective of 3-4 lines is usual
australia_nz.references: two referees, often with contact details, or 'available on request'

letter.focus: the role's key requirements; public sector and universities ask for a separate statement addressing each selection criterion

notes: Selection criteria statements (often 1-2 pages, one heading per criterion, with concrete examples) are common for government and university jobs.

france.label: France and French-speaking postings
france.spelling: French if the posting is in French; British or US English otherwise
france.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, city; age and photo optional
france.work_authorization: state it if you are not an EU/EEA citizen
france.profile_section: a one-line title and a short profile are usual

letter.closing: formal closing formula in French letters (Je vous prie d'agréer...); 'Kind regards,' in English
letter.focus: lettre de motivation: you, them, us; formal register

france.language: French postings expect French documents unless English is stated

benelux.label: Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg
benelux.spelling: British or US English used consistently; Dutch/French/German if the posting is in it
benelux.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, city; date of birth optional
benelux.work_authorization: state it if you are not an EU/EEA citizen
benelux.tone: direct, concise and to the point (especially in the Netherlands)

letter.focus: short and specific: why this job, what you bring

benelux.language: Dutch postings in the Netherlands often accept English for technical roles; Belgian postings follow the region's language

southern_europe.label: Spain, Italy, Portugal, Greece, Malta, Cyprus
southern_europe.spelling: British English (or the local language if the posting is in it)
southern_europe.personal_details: name, phone, e-mail, city; date of birth and nationality traditional but optional
southern_europe.work_authorization: state it if you are not an EU/EEA citizen

letter.focus: formal motivation letter

data_consent_clause.IT: Autorizzo il trattamento dei dati personali contenuti nel mio curriculum vitae in base al Regolamento UE 2016/679 (GDPR).

notes: In Italy a data-processing consent sentence at the end of the CV is customary; Europass format is common in the public sector.

central_eastern.label: Central and Eastern Europe and the Baltics
central_eastern.spelling: British or US English used consistently; the local language if the posting is in it
central_eastern.work_authorization: state it if you are not an EU/EEA citizen

letter.focus: formal motivation letter

central_eastern.language: the posting's language; English is common for international companies

data_consent_clause.PL: I agree to the processing of personal data provided in this document for realising the recruitment process pursuant to the Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (GDPR).

notes: In Poland a GDPR consent sentence at the end of the CV is customary and often requested in the posting.

international.label: Other or unknown country (neutral international style)
international.spelling: British or US English used consistently

letter.focus: fit with the role

phd.label: PhD position
phd.emphasis: Preparation and potential: the degree, thesis, relevant courses and grades, methods and tools learned, and a clear interest in this project's topic.
phd.wording: Modest and curious. Describe what you did and learned in projects; do not claim expertise. 'I would like to contribute to' rather than 'I will lead'.

sections.heading: Research Interests
sections.focus: two or three lines tying your background to the project's topic

sections.heading: Education
sections.focus: degree, thesis title and supervisor, relevant courses and grades

sections.heading: Research and Thesis Projects
sections.focus: what each project asked, your own part, methods, result

sections.heading: Publications
sections.focus: only if you have any; exact as published

sections.heading: Experience
sections.focus: internships, teaching assistant or relevant part-time work

sections.heading: Technical Skills
sections.focus: tools and methods the project names, with where you used them

sections.heading: References
sections.focus: two referees, for example the thesis supervisor

letter.focus: Why this project and group, which courses or thesis work prepared you for it, what you want to learn, and your research interest.

postdoc.label: Postdoc
postdoc.emphasis: PhD results and their impact, publications, the methods you master, growing independence, and fit with the group's projects.
postdoc.wording: State your own contributions clearly ('I designed', 'I led the tape-out') while crediting co-authors. Neither modest nor inflated.

sections.heading: Research Profile
sections.focus: three or four lines: field, main results, what you bring to this group

sections.heading: Research Experience
sections.focus: PhD and research positions: topic, your contributions, results

sections.heading: Education
sections.focus: PhD: thesis title, supervisor, year; earlier degrees briefly

sections.heading: Publications
sections.focus: complete list, grouped by journal and conference, your name marked

sections.heading: Teaching and Supervision
sections.focus: courses and supervised students

sections.heading: Technical Skills
sections.focus: methods and tools relevant to the group's work

sections.heading: References
sections.focus: two or three referees with title, affiliation and e-mail

letter.focus: Fit with the group's research, your main PhD results, what you would work on there, and what you would bring.

research_assistant.label: Research assistant / engineer (university or research centre)
research_assistant.emphasis: Hands-on skills that support a research group: implementation, lab and measurement work, tools, reliability and documentation.
research_assistant.wording: Concrete and practical: what you built, ran, measured or maintained, and for whom.

sections.heading: Experience
sections.focus: lab, research-engineering and development work; your own part

sections.heading: Technical Skills
sections.focus: tools, languages, lab equipment, with where you used them

sections.heading: Publications
sections.focus: if any; contributions to papers count

letter.focus: Which tasks of the group you can take on from day one, the tools you know, and how you work with researchers.

assistant_professor.label: Assistant professor / tenure track
assistant_professor.emphasis: An independent research line and plan, funding record or potential, teaching experience and pedagogical training, and supervision.
assistant_professor.wording: Confident about your research vision, backed by evidence. Reflect on teaching instead of only listing courses.

sections.heading: Research Profile
sections.focus: your research line and where you take it next

sections.heading: Grants and Funding
sections.focus: funding you received or co-wrote, with amounts and your role

sections.heading: Publications
sections.focus: complete list, grouped by type, your name marked

sections.heading: Supervision
sections.focus: PhD and master students, your role, outcomes

sections.heading: Teaching Experience
sections.focus: courses, your role, development work

sections.heading: Pedagogical Training
sections.focus: university teaching courses (in Sweden: högskolepedagogik)

sections.heading: Academic Service
sections.focus: reviewing, committees, organisation

letter.focus: Your research vision and how it fits the department, funding plans, your teaching approach, and supervision.

professor.label: Associate or full professor
professor.emphasis: Research leadership and programme, funding, international standing, supervision record, and pedagogical and administrative merits.
professor.wording: Authoritative and factual: let the record speak. Quantify funding, graduated students and leadership roles.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.focus: research programme, leadership and standing

sections.heading: Research Leadership
sections.focus: groups, centres and projects you lead

sections.heading: Grants and Funding
sections.focus: as principal investigator, with amounts

sections.heading: Publications
sections.focus: selected publications first, then the complete list

sections.heading: Supervision
sections.focus: PhD students graduated and current, postdocs

sections.heading: Academic Service and Assignments
sections.focus: boards, evaluation committees, editorships

sections.heading: Collaboration and Impact
sections.focus: industry, society, patents

sections.heading: References
sections.focus: usually not listed at this level unless asked

letter.focus: Your research programme and its future, leadership, funding, and what you would build in the department.

lecturer.label: Lecturer (university)
lecturer.emphasis: Teaching record, course development, pedagogical training and student supervision; research as support for teaching.
lecturer.wording: Reflective and student-centred, with concrete teaching examples (what you changed in a course and why).

sections.heading: Teaching Experience
sections.focus: courses, level, your role, number of students

sections.heading: Course Development
sections.focus: courses or labs you designed or renewed

sections.heading: Supervision
sections.focus: thesis students

sections.heading: Publications
sections.focus: selected

sections.heading: Languages
sections.focus: teaching languages

letter.focus: How you teach and why, courses you can give, course development, and how your research supports teaching.

internship.label: Internship or thesis project
internship.emphasis: Studies, relevant courses and projects, eagerness to learn, and when and how long you are available.
internship.wording: Plain and keen: what you learned and built in courses and projects. No inflated titles.

sections.heading: Profile
sections.focus: programme, year, and what you want to work on

sections.heading: Education
sections.focus: current programme, relevant courses, expected graduation

sections.heading: Projects
sections.focus: course and personal projects with the tools the posting names

sections.heading: Experience
sections.focus: part-time jobs and student roles

letter.focus: Why this company and project, the courses or projects that prepared you, and your available dates.

junior.label: Junior / graduate
junior.emphasis: Foundation: degree and thesis, internships, and projects that used the tools named in the posting; how fast you learn.
junior.wording: Modest but clear about what you did yourself. Describe tasks and results, not personal qualities.

sections.heading: Education
sections.focus: degree and thesis

sections.heading: Work Experience
sections.focus: internships and first roles

letter.focus: Why this employer and team, the experience closest to the posting, and what you want to grow into.

mid_senior.label: Experienced / mid-senior
mid_senior.emphasis: Results delivered in recent roles, ownership of blocks or modules, and the tools and flows the posting names.
mid_senior.wording: Matter-of-fact and specific: 'designed', 'verified', 'delivered'. Confident without superlatives.

sections.heading: Work Experience
sections.focus: recent roles in detail, older roles shorter

sections.heading: Selected Publications
sections.focus: only for research-oriented roles

letter.focus: The two or three experiences closest to the posting, your own part in them, and why this team.

senior.label: Senior / staff / lead
senior.emphasis: Scope and ownership: systems or products you were responsible for, technical decisions, leading and mentoring, cross-team work, tape-outs or launches.
senior.wording: Confident and direct: 'led', 'owned', 'defined', always backed by what happened.

sections.heading: Summary
sections.focus: three or four lines on scope and expertise

sections.heading: Professional Experience
sections.focus: scope, decisions and outcomes; early roles in one line

sections.heading: Selected Projects
sections.focus: two or three projects that match the posting

letter.focus: What you would own and improve in this role, backed by the closest results you led.

confidence.1: very modest: understate; let facts speak quietly
confidence.2: modest: plain statements, credit others, no claims of expertise
confidence.3: balanced: clear about your own contributions, no superlatives
confidence.4: confident: lead with ownership and results
confidence.5: assertive: strong action verbs, impact first (still only what the material verifies)

lengths.short: brief: one to three lines, or one or two bullets
lengths.normal: usual: three or four lines or bullets per entry
lengths.detailed: in depth: five or six bullets for recent entries
